prediction.text: In June 2025, just before its fiscal 2025 year-end, P&G announced a multi-year restructuring program covering fiscal 2026 and 2027. It would eliminate up to about 7,000 non-manufacturing roles, roughly 6-7% of that workforce, over two years. It would also exit certain brands, categories, and sub-markets in selected countries. The company said the goal was to simplify the organization, with broader roles, clearer accountability, and faster decision-making, and to focus resources on its core businesses and markets to support productivity and growth amid a tough, uncertain consumer and cost environment. P&G also said it expected the program to produce one-time before-tax charges of roughly $1.0-$1.6 billion, mostly severance and some asset write-downs, on top of its usual restructuring spending. I'm going from memory on the exact charge range and breakdown, so check the fiscal 2025 10-K's restructuring note for precise figures.
